minutes.summary: The committee heard an actuary on retiree health liability and a financial advisor on debt service for the TC Passios and Turkey Hill projects, then fire and police chiefs presented FY22 budget requests. The town manager walked through changes from the target to preliminary budget. The committee approved the February 11 minutes and adjourned.

topics.topic: Opening, open meeting law reminder, public hearing logistics
Public comment on fully burdened department budgets and health insurance
Debt projections for TC Passios and Turkey Hill
Town manager and finance director reports, budget adjustments, vaccine update
Committee reports, school committee updates and fire alarm earmark

what_happened.line: The committee heard an actuary on the town's retiree health (OPEB) liability, which grows as interest rates fall and is backed by small trust assets.
A financial advisor modeled debt service for the TC Passios and Turkey Hill projects and found both within town debt policy.
The town manager, finance director and debt advisor agreed to translate the TC Passios debt into a tax rate effect.
The fire and police chiefs presented FY22 budget requests; both were informational, with no vote taken.
The committee approved the February 11 minutes and adjourned, setting March 4 for Monty Tech, DPW and a first look at draft warrant articles.

why_it_matters: Retiree health liability and new school and building debt both draw on future tax bills, and the tax-rate translation of the TC Passios debt is the figure residents will most need to weigh.
The school budget carries health insurance differently from town departments, so year-to-year department comparisons can mislead until fully burdened costs are produced.
watch_next: March 4 meeting at seven: Monty Tech, DPW and a first look at draft warrant articles.
The tax-rate impact of the TC Passios debt, to be produced by the town manager, finance director and debt advisor.
